rule.title: Hoboken rent control base-rent freeze
rule.requirement: A landlord may not charge rent above what the landlord was receiving on the chapter's effective date, nor above the rent received on January 11, 1973 where that exceeds the rent authorized by this chapter.
rule.key_value: rents capped at those received on the chapter's effective date and on January 11, 1973
rule.coverage_conditions: Dwellings subject to Chapter 155 of the Hoboken City Code; no building age, size or owner limits are stated in this section.
rule.penalty: Violation of Chapter 155 is punishable under N.J.S.A. 40:49-5, including a fine not exceeding $2,000; each dwelling unit is a separate violation.
rule.quoted_span:
No landlord shall, after the effective date of this chapter, charge any rents in excess of what he was
     receiving from the effective date of this chapter; nor shall such landlord charge any rents in excess
     of what he was receiving on January 11, 1973, if such excess is in excess of the rental which is
     authorized by this chapter.

rule.title: Hoboken vacancy decontrol increase cap
rule.requirement: On a tenant's voluntary vacancy of a registered apartment, the unit is decontrolled for the new tenant's initial rent, capped at a 25% increase over the last rent paid, excluding any capital improvement surcharge; decontrol is limited to once every three years.
rule.key_value: 25% over last rent; decontrol at most once per 3 years
rule.coverage_conditions: Rental apartment units registered under §155-30 that are covered by Chapter 155; decontrol requires voluntary vacancy without harassment, duress or pressure, or a legal eviction or court order.
rule.exemptions: The decontrolled apartment unit is exempt from Chapter 155 for the new tenant's initial rental only.
rule.penalty: The Board may rescind an improper decontrol, revert the rent, and prosecute the landlord under §155-21 (fine up to $2,000).
rule.quoted_span:
provided, however, that said
     rental shall be limited to an increase of 25% over the last rental paid by the tenant who voluntarily
     vacated the rental unit, exclusive of any capital improvement surcharge that is a component of

rule.title: Hoboken rent control ordinance — rent increase limits
rule.requirement: Rents are controlled at the base rent level received as of October 1, 1985; no rent increase may be charged unless allowed by this chapter, and a landlord seeking an increase must give the tenant written notice at least 30 days before it takes effect.
rule.coverage_conditions: All dwelling units, except motels/hotels, newly constructed dwellings at first rental, industrial and nonresidential/commercial property, school/college student housing, government-owned housing, buildings vacant since January 1, 1984, and multiple dwellings built after June 25, 1987 under N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.1.
rule.exemptions: Motels and hotels; newly constructed dwellings at first rental; industrial property; nonresidential and commercial units; school/college student housing; government-owned housing; buildings vacant since January 1, 1984; multiple dwellings constructed after June 25, 1987 (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.1).
rule.penalty: Rent increases above those allowed are null and void; excess rents must be refunded or credited to the tenant.
rule.interaction: Chapter application is preempted while a governmental agency contract regulates the rents, and resumes after the contract terminates.
rule.quoted_span:
All rents for rental of housing space and services in dwellings to which this act is applicable
     are hereby controlled at the base rent level received by the landlord as of October 1, 1985, and
     no rental increases shall be hereinafter demanded, paid or accepted, except as provided in this
     chapter.

rule.title: Hoboken algorithmic rent fixing prohibition
rule.requirement: A landlord renting a residential dwelling unit in Hoboken may not price fix using algorithmic pricing, meaning software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms that collect and analyze nonpublic competitor information from other lessors to coordinate, recommend or implement rental prices, lease terms or occupancy levels.
rule.coverage_conditions: Landlords renting any residential dwelling unit in Hoboken; a residential dwelling unit is any primary residence excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities.
rule.exemptions: Medical/long-term care and detention facilities are excluded from the definition of residential dwelling unit.
rule.penalty: Penalties under N.J.S.A. 40:49-5, or a fine not exceeding $2,000, or community service not exceeding 90 days.
rule.quoted_span: Landlords who rent any residential dwelling unit (defined as any primary residence excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities) in the City of Hoboken are prohibited from price fixing using algorithmic pricing.

sources.quoted_span: Landlords who rent any residential dwelling unit (defined as any primary residence excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities) in the City of Hoboken are prohibited from price fixing using algorithmic pricing.

rule.title: Hoboken Rent Leveling and Stabilization Ordinance — Board approval for rent increases
rule.requirement: A landlord must obtain Rent Leveling and Stabilization Board approval before imposing any rent increase, including a hardship increase. A tenant may seek a rent decrease from the Board when services, care or maintenance decline.
rule.coverage_conditions: Dwellings covered by Article II of Chapter 155, except newly constructed dwellings and buildings completely vacant since January 1, 1984, whose exemption eligibility the Regulation Officer and Rent Regulation Officer determine.
rule.exemptions: Newly constructed dwellings and buildings completely vacant since January 1, 1984, with eligibility determined by the Regulation Officer and the Rent Regulation Officer respectively.
rule.quoted_span:
In the event that a landlord cannot meet his operating expenses or does not make a fair return
           on his investment, he may appeal to the Rent Leveling and Stabilization Board for a hardship
           rental increase. No landlord shall impose upon any tenant an increase in rent under this
           Article without first obtaining approval with the Board.

rule.title: Hoboken Rent Leveling and Stabilization Ordinance rent increase cap
rule.requirement: A landlord may not raise rent by more than 5% or the CPI percentage differential, whichever is less, nor more than once in any 12-month period; tax, water/sewer and capital-improvement surcharges require approval.
rule.coverage_conditions: Rental dwellings under the Hoboken Rent Leveling and Stabilization chapter; newly constructed dwellings and buildings completely vacant since January 1, 1984 may be exempt.
rule.exemptions: Newly constructed dwellings and buildings completely vacant since January 1, 1984 may be exempt, with eligibility determined by the Regulation Officer or Rent Regulation Officer.
rule.penalty: Excess rent increases are void and excess rents must be refunded or credited to the tenant.
rule.quoted_span:
At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of a lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord
     may request or receive a percentage increase in rent which is greater than 5% or the percentage
     difference between the consumer price index three months prior to the expiration or termination
     of the lease and three months prior to the commencement of the lease term, whichever is less.
